name: Norse longhouse with a turf roof

versions.summary: Stylized Norse longhouse matching the reference: vertical-plank wooden walls on stone footings, dark gable end with extruded triangle and plank lines, grass (moss-textured) twin-slope living roof with ridge cap and eave batten rows, stone chimney with twin dark arched openings, carved X-cross gable with spiral volute tops and inlay studs, S-scroll eave finials with ball tips, and seeded scatter of grass tufts, leaf sprigs and flowers on the roof. Code is now a bare body (no anonymous function statement) so it parses; all parts use valid types, finite coords, and LOD hints; ~150 parts across 7 named objects.

review.summary: The current geometry fails to match the reference's silhouette and cohesion. The most critical failure is the roof, which intersects in an 'X' shape rather than forming a peak. Secondary issues include disconnected floating elements (finials, grass) and a wall structure that reads as a fence rather than a solid building.
issues: Reposition and re-rotate the roof planes so they meet at a central ridge and slope downward to the eaves, eliminating the incorrect 'X' intersection seen in the side and back views.
Redesign the eave finials to be physically connected to the roof corners and shaped like the carved scrolls in the reference, removing the currently floating spheres.
Replace the scattered, floating grass ellipsoids with a continuous, cohesive geometry layer on the roof surface to properly simulate a living roof.
Adjust the side wall construction to read as a solid structure; ensure the dark wood backing is fully visible and cohesive with the exterior planks rather than looking like an open fence.
Tighten the alignment of the gable cross, door, and front framing so they sit flush against the front wall without floating gaps or disjointed parts.

versions.summary: Rebuilt as a cohesive Norse longhouse: corrected gabled roof planes now meet at a central ridge; solid dark-wood side and gable walls replace the fence look; continuous grass roof slabs and ridge turf replace floating tufts; eave scrolls are connected corner brackets; front gable cross, door, and framing are tightened flush. Seeded variation is used only for roof flora placement.

review.summary: The model reads clearly as a Norse longhouse with a living roof. Front and back gables show the carved triangular end with apex spiral volutes, a horizontal tie beam, light carved diagonals, and a dark door opening on the front; the long sides display vertical dark-plank infill between light timber posts sitting on grey stone pilings; the pitched roof is covered in green turf with scattered grass tufts, leaf sprigs and pale blossoms; a twin-flued stone chimney with a cap rises off-center from the slope; and carved finials mark the four eave corners. Silhouette, proportions, part placement and material separation (wood / stone / turf / carved accents) are coherent and match the reference's overall composition, making it a recognizable, complete interpretation at the requested complexity.
